groups.label: Searchable text corpora
groups.description: Collections of Sanskrit etexts. They overlap with the sources MEOBTIS indexes, or hold little Buddhist material in a form we can republish.

items.name: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS)
items.summary: A morphologically and lexically analysed corpus of Sanskrit, searchable by word, lemma and grammatical form. Its data is on GitHub under CC BY 4.0. The Buddhist texts we noticed in it are the Bodhicaryāvatāra and the Saundarananda, both already in MEOBTIS.
items.why: It is a linguistic corpus, not a set of readable editions, and its Buddhist texts are already indexed from GRETIL and DSBC.

items.name: Ambuda
items.summary: A reading environment for Sanskrit texts with a proofreading workflow, dictionaries and parsing aids.
items.why: We could not confirm which Buddhist texts it holds, so it is listed here as a reading tool rather than indexed.

items.name: Muktabodha Digital Library
items.summary: A large digital library of Sanskrit manuscripts and etexts, strongest in Śaiva and tantric literature.
items.access: Freely available; terms are given per text
items.why: Its holdings are mainly Hindu tantric, and we could not confirm a body of Buddhist texts we could republish.

items.name: Searchable Aggregate Library of Sanskrit Etexts
items.summary: An aggregate of Sanskrit etexts from many sources in one searchable library, announced on the Indology list in February 2026 with about 1,500 etexts.
items.why: It brings together etexts from other collections, so we index the original sources instead.

groups.label: Scholarly editions and transcriptions
groups.description: Editions published by research projects, usually as PDFs or wiki pages, with no licence that lets us convert and republish them.

items.name: Institute for Advanced Buddhology, Soka University (IRIAB)
items.summary: Publishes the annual report ARIRIAB, the Bibliotheca Philologica et Philosophica Buddhica series, the British Library and St Petersburg Sanskrit fragment series, and the facsimile edition of the Gilgit manuscripts in the National Archives of India, edited by Oskar von Hinüber, Seishi Karashima and Noriyuki Kudo. DSBC cites ARIRIAB (Soka University, 2013) as the source of some of its texts.
items.access: PDFs from the institute's website; each article is marked © IRIAB, Soka University, and we found no licence statement
items.why: We would need the institute's permission before reusing its transcriptions. Its website could not be reached when we last checked, so the link below is the announcement on the Indology list.

contents.label: Sanskrit text editions in the annual report (ARIRIAB)
contents.note: Compiled from the report's contents lists for volumes I–XXIX (1998–2026); volume and year in brackets. Most are transcriptions of single manuscripts or fragments. Material in Gāndhārī, Khotanese, Tocharian, Uyghur, Tibetan and Chinese is left out.

items.name: Saktumiva wiki: Gilgit Samādhirājasūtra
items.summary: A transcription of the Gilgit manuscript of the Samādhirājasūtra, made from the 2018 facsimile edition by Kudo and colleagues, with variant readings from other witnesses.
items.access: Free to read online; no licence stated
items.why: Specialist transcription with no licence, and a different editorial method from the readable editions we index.

items.name: Taishō University: Vinayasūtra
items.summary: A romanised edition of Guṇaprabha's Vinayasūtra, published as a PDF by Taishō University.
items.why: The Vinayasūtra is already indexed from GRETIL and DSBC. Taishō University's Potala edition of the Vimalakīrtinirdeśa (2006) is also in DSBC.

items.name: Lotus Sūtra Manuscript Series
items.summary: Critical transcriptions and photographs of Sanskrit manuscripts of the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka (Lotus Sūtra), edited by Kotsuki Chikako. Volumes were issued in 2019 and 2023.
items.access: Printed volumes; see the notice of the series
items.why: Printed scholarly volumes rather than a free digital text.

groups.label: Manuscript collections and images
groups.description: Digitised manuscripts and facsimiles. These are images of the originals, not texts, so there is nothing for us to convert.

items.name: Schøyen Collection: Buddhist manuscripts
items.summary: A private collection with early Sanskrit Buddhist manuscripts, including an Aśoka legend (6th century), Abhidharma texts, a Mahāsaṃghika-Lokottaravāda Pratimokṣa-vibhaṅga, Bamiyan birch-bark manuscripts of the Bhaiṣajyaguru and Vajracchedikā, and a Guhyasamāja and Saṃpuṭodbhava Tantra manuscript of 1801. They are edited in Braarvig (ed.), Buddhist Manuscripts in the Schøyen Collection, four volumes published by Hermes in Oslo, 2000–2016, with editions of about 55 texts and fragments in Sanskrit and Gāndhārī, among them a Kuṣāṇa-period Aṣṭasāhasrikā, the Vajracchedikā, Samādhirāja and Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha, and a Gāndhārī Ekottarikāgama and Bodhisattvapiṭaka. The publisher offers all four volumes, and the exhibition catalogue Traces of Gandharan Buddhism, as free PDF downloads.
items.access: Catalogue entries and images online; the printed editions free to download as PDF
items.why: The volumes are free to download but marked all rights reserved, so we cannot republish converted text without the publisher's permission. They are also editions of fragments with introductions, translations and notes, not continuous texts. One exception is indexed: the Sanskrit of the Sarvadharmāpravṛttinirdeśa from volume i (see Sources).

contents.label: Texts edited in the volumes that MEOBTIS does not index
contents.note: All are fragments, not complete texts. Titles follow the volumes' tables of contents; the volume number is given in brackets.

items.name: British Library Endangered Archives Programme: Nepal
items.summary: Digitisation projects that photographed Sanskrit manuscripts held in Nepal, many of them Newar Buddhist: EAP676, EAP790 and EAP1023 (478 manuscripts from 28 collections, 10th to 18th centuries). Shanker Thapa has separately surveyed about 1,285 manuscripts from 67 collections.
items.access: Free images; EAP's reuse terms are CC BY-NC where the material is in copyright

items.name: Cambridge University Library: Bendall collection
items.summary: Manuscripts collected in Nepal by Cecil Bendall in the 1880s, many of them Buddhist, held by Cambridge University Library. Bendall's 1883 catalogue of the Buddhist Sanskrit manuscripts is available from the Wellcome Collection.
items.access: Free images; the catalogue is public domain
items.why: Images and a catalogue only, with no transcriptions.

groups.label: Tools, parallels and dictionaries
groups.description: Resources for reading and comparing the texts, not collections of editions.

items.name: BuddhaNexus
items.summary: A search and comparison tool from the University of Hamburg and the Khyentse Center that finds parallel passages across Sanskrit, Pali, Tibetan and Chinese Buddhist texts. Its Sanskrit comes largely from GRETIL.
items.why: A comparison tool; its Sanskrit is already indexed here from GRETIL.

items.name: SuttaCentral
items.summary: A site for the early Buddhist discourses, mainly in Pali, with translations and parallels. It includes Sanskrit fragments, marked "Skt frgm".
items.why: Mainly Pali and translations; the Sanskrit it holds is fragmentary.

items.name: Sanskrit Dictionary of the Buddhist Texts from the Turfan Finds
items.summary: A dictionary of the Sanskrit of the Buddhist manuscripts found at Turfan, produced by the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities. The Berlin-Brandenburg Academy's Turfan project describes the collection the manuscripts come from.
items.access: Project pages online; the dictionary is a printed work
items.why: A dictionary and a manuscript project, not a set of etexts.
